messages:
alex: heads-up — we've got a customer escalation: p95/p99 latency spike for /v1/generate in prod-us-west. Customers reporting slow responses and timeouts since ~15:03 UTC. SLOs show p95 ~420ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~1.1s -> 3.8s. stack: redwood-34b-quant (primary).

maria: :eyes: any recent deploys or config flips? which tenants affected — single org or broad?

alex: no deploys in the last hour. spike correlates with a handful of heavy streaming sessions from tenant=acme-inc (high concurrency). reproducer curl below, I can share logs.

alex: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-34b-quant","input":"summarize this...","max_tokens":1024}'
```

alex: sample tail of logs (truncated):
```
[15:03:12] req_id=abc123 route=/v1/generate queued_ms=120 inflight=48 kernel_wait=310 model_exec_ms=980
[15:03:13] req_id=def456 queued_ms=95 inflight=51 model_exec_ms=1100 error=null
[15:03:14] req_id=ghi789 queued_ms=210 inflight=60 model_exec_ms=2400 warn=kv-cache-miss
```

jon: likely overloaded GPU tails + some requests hitting cold kv-cache. Immediate mitigation options: (1) route ACME to fallback smaller model (8b-slim) in us-west, (2) apply short circuit-breaker for per-tenant p99 > 1s to drop/redirect, (3) temp rate-limit heavy API keys.

maria: agree. Plan: 1) enable model fallback for path /v1/generate -> redwood-8b-slim (preserve semantics), 2) set circuit-breaker p99 threshold 900ms for tenant-scoped policy, 3) add a soft 20rps token bucket for that tenant. jon, can you apply the routing? sam, can you handle the rate-limit? I'll configure the CB.

jon: applying routing now. using rictl:
```bash
rictl routing update --path /v1/generate --match-tenant acme-inc \n  --fallback-model redwood-8b-slim --region us-west --priority 10
```
jon: done — traffic for acme-inc should start shifting within ~10s. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: automation: routing-change accepted (change_id=chg-20260316-77). Rolling update to edge proxies.

maria: setting CB:
```bash
rictl guardrail set-cb --scope tenant:acme-inc --path /v1/generate --metric p99_latency_ms --threshold 900 --action fallback
```
maria: CB applied, first check window 60s.

sam: I added a temporary tenant-specific rate-limit on api-key (acme-prod-key): 20rps burst 40 via rate-limiter service. rules id rl-332.

sre-bot: rate-limit applied (rl-332). Observability: new metrics will be visible in Console > Rate Limits > rl-332.

lina: I'm watching metrics now — within 2mins p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 470ms, p99 down to ~780ms. Great.

alex: customers on the thread reporting improved response times. I'll keep the ticket open until stable for 1h. We should also capture a repro and add a mitigation playbook entry.

jon: quick notes for post-incident: root cause hypothesis = KV-cache pressure + request composition causing long model execs on 34b quant; fallback to 8b-slim reduces runtime and KV pressure. Next actions: (A) add test that simulates ACME workload on staging to reproduce tail, (B) look at autoscaling thresholds for quant models (lower the scale-up threshold for inflight>40), (C) evaluate enabling warm-KV prefetch for long sessions.

maria: agreed. I'll open a GH issue with actionable tasks and link perf graphs. tagging eng-runtime and ml-infra. assign to jon for the autoscale tweak, lina for KV prefetch spike test, alex for customer comms.

alex: customer comms: pinged ACME PM with summary and ETA for follow-up. they're ok with current fallback but want a durable fix.

sam: temp config notes for rollback: rl-332 can be revoked with `rictl rate-limit delete rl-332` and routing change reversed with the change id. keep changes for 1h then re-evaluate.

maria: logging this as incident-2026-03-16-latency-005. I'll start a postmortem draft after 60m stable window. Thanks team. :pray:

alex: closing loop — monitoring for 1h, will update ticket and signal when we can revert or promote permanent guardrail.

lina: ack. keeping an eye on kv-cache miss rate and model exec histograms.

sre-bot: incident-2026-03-16-latency-005: status=monitoring.

jon: one last note — consider adding an automated rollback for heavy tenants: if tenant p95 > 1s for >2m, auto-switch to fallback model + notify oncall. low-friction patch could avoid manual steps next time.

alex: +1. I'll add that to the GH issue.

maria: good work all.
